For MLB, 37.5 effective picks/week over 37 weeks (~1387.5 picks) suffice; for NFL, 9.2 picks/week over 152 weeks (~1398.4 picks) suffice. This implies a fundamental asymmetry in operational cadence. The NFL cannot certify solo due to its high-frequency, low-correlation structure, while MLB’s lower frequency allows for longer certification windows. Preseason exclusion is enforced because N_eff for preseason is orders of magnitude smaller than regular season, making it non-certifiable. The key-number handling avoids distortion by operating in price space, where Δ = no-vig close - no-vig entry already accounts for jump probabilities. These primitives form a dual logic: one for operational planning (certification timeline), one for data integrity (preseason exclusion).
